messages.subject: scan() followed by if statement
parts:
Hello,

I have just recently begun working through QCLwR and have a question.

In "Exercise box 3.3: Conditional expressions" we are asked to

"Write a few lines of code in an editor that 'educates' a user to
enter 4 at the prompt. First, the script prompts the user to input the
number 4 (use scan as mentioned in Section 3.2.2). Second, a
conditional expression tests whether the user did enter 4 or not. If
the user entered 4, the output should say "Good!" - if not, the output
should say "Dummy, this is not 4. Enter 4 when you are prompted
again!", and then the user is prompted to enter 4 again. Another
conditional expression follows whether the user entered 4 this time.
If yes, the output should read "Thanks, now it is right.", if not, the
output should read "You will never learn ...".

I keep getting an error message after the first few lines of my
script:

> x<-scan(quiet=T)
1: if (x==4)
Error in scan(file, what, nmax, sep, dec, quote, skip, nlines,
na.strings, :
scan() expected 'a real', got 'if'
> {cat("Good!")}

After trying a number of different things (adding different arguments
to scan, for example) without success I fell back to the answer key.
However, when entering the answer key script:

aa<-scan(nmax=1, quiet=T)
if (aa==4) {
cat("Good! ")
} else {
cat("Dummy, this is not 4. Enter 4 when you are prompted again! ")
aa<-scan(nmax=1, quiet=T)
if (aa==4) {
cat("Thanks, now it is right. ")
} else {
cat("You will never learn Â… ")
}
}

I continued to get the same error message:

> aa<-scan(nmax=1, quiet=T)
1: if (aa==4) {
Error in scan(file, what, nmax, sep, dec, quote, skip, nlines,
na.strings, :
scan() expected 'a real', got 'if'
> cat("Good! ")
Good!
....

I have some experience with BASIC and C++ and it could be that I'm
having trouble getting used to R's command line interface (as opposed
to compiling and running programs like in other languages). Were we
not meant to paste the entire script from the editor into the GUI? Or
do we have to paste the different sections in separately in order to
allow R time to receive user input from scan()? Or, is there some
kind of a "pause" function that will tell R to wait for user input
before moving on to the if statement? Right now it looks like R is
assigning the if statement to where the user's input should be.

Any thoughts or advice on this would be appreciated.

Thanks very much.

Take care,

D. Thomas
Meiji Gakuin University, Yokohama, Japan

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] scan() followed by if statement
parts:
The input of the number has to be a separate input from the
conditional expression, otherwise the beginning of the conditional
expression ('if (...) {" is parsed as the input to scan, and since
scan expects a number but gets a character string, it crashes. Hence
either you paste this

############## copy here
aa<-scan(nmax=1, quiet=T)
4

if (aa==4) {
cat("Good! ")
} else {
cat("Dummy, this is not 4. Enter 4 when you are prompted again! ")
aa<-scan(nmax=1, quiet=T)
if (aa==4) {
cat("Thanks, now it is right. ")
} else {
cat("You will never learn Â… ")
}
}

############## till here

and get the output in the attachment, or you proceed in two steps,
more manually:

############## copy here
aa<-scan(nmax=1, quiet=T) ############## till here

then you enter

4

then you copy/paste the rest:

############## copy here

if (aa==4) {
cat("Good! ")
} else {
cat("Dummy, this is not 4. Enter 4 when you are prompted again! ")
aa<-scan(nmax=1, quiet=T)
if (aa==4) {
cat("Thanks, now it is right. ")
} else {
cat("You will never learn Â… ")
}
}

############## till here

This opens up another question though.  If the if statement is being parsed as the input to scan in the first instance of scan() why don't we get an error message in the second instance where the if statement follows scan()?  In the second case, it seems that the if statement is not being parsed as input. 

Thanks for your help.  Much appreciated.

Take care,

D. Thomas

parts:
Thanks for your quick replies.  Ok.  I see that in one case we're outside the conditional and in the other case we're inside the conditional.  But relative to each other the scan() function and the if statement are together in both cases.  Why would scan read the if(...) string as input when it's outside {...} but not when it's inside?  Is this just a strange quirk in the language? Maybe something to do with scope? Or is there something specific I'm missing here? 

I hate to trouble this forum with such a small problem but I've googled the topic (and even looked through a copy of Crawley's The R Book) but can't seem to find out why this would be the case.   I know it's not a big thing, but it's kind of been bothering me all day.  :-)

Thanks again for your comments.

Take care,
D
